A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThinKV and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–H. Content can be matched across the section reorganization, renumbering, and moves between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, throughput, attention-pattern, and ablation results, including Figure 8, Tables 1–4, and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds serving measurements, sensitivity analyses, Qwen3 experiments, and LongBench v2 evaluation.

M1.justification: Appendix E.16 adds an optional composite procedure using SnapKV eviction of quantized prefill tokens before ThinKV decoding. This extends the compression pipeline for long inputs. The core thought decomposition, TBQ, TBE, calibration algorithm, and Continuous Thinking procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds LongBench v2's Code Repo QA subtask, covering long-input/long-output reasoning with 16K–32K-token inputs and outputs up to 8K tokens (E.16). Existing mathematics, code-generation, GSM8K, and LongWriter coverage is retained. The added Qwen3 experiments reuse LiveCodeBench.

E2.justification: v2 introduces a non-thinking FullKV comparator for Qwen3-8B (Table 13) and adds TBE to the generation-length comparison (Figure 10(d), formerly Figure 9(d)). The principal eviction and quantization baseline sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled vLLM and concurrent-request evaluations, fixed-batch component measurements, additional cache-budget sweeps, Qwen3 thinking-mode comparisons, and request-latency and Intelligence/Watt metrics. It also reattributes the retained LiveCodeBench precision-ablation plot from R1-Llama-8B to R1-Llama-70B; this reported setting revision does not establish that the experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The accuracy-only component ablation in v1 Table 3 becomes a broader accuracy/throughput/latency analysis with additional TBE budgets in v2 Table 4. New analyses examine separate K/V quantization sensitivity by thought type, accuracy–memory frontiers, overhead across batch sizes, thinking versus non-thinking behavior, and compatibility with SnapKV (E.9 and E.11–E.16).

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies eight independent responses per question for pass@1 estimation and averaging throughput and latency over three independent runs (6.1). This is newly reported sampling information, not evidence of increased run counts. The existing 50-rollout thought-importance analysis is retained; confidence intervals and significance tests are not added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 8 retain their numerical results, but substantial additional results appear. Examples include vLLM throughput of 6622.4 for ThinKV versus 4883.3 for R-KV (ovl) at batch 256 (Table 12), and Code Repo QA accuracy of 28 versus FullKV's 30 with the 4096-token SnapKV prefill budget (Table 15). Further additions cover Qwen3, component performance, sensitivity, generation length, and request latency.

T1.justification: The thought-decomposition and compression formulations, calibration mathematics, and Appendix C permutation-invariance theorem and proof are retained. Renaming Definitions 2–3 as Problem Formulations 1–2 does not alter their mathematics. The added standard pass@1 formula introduces no new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same four contributions and headline claims: thought-adaptive hybrid compression, efficient memory-slot reuse, near-lossless accuracy below 5% of the original cache, and throughput improvements up to 5.8×. The additions primarily provide further support.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking K/V sensitivity to precision assignments and component performance to generation-length inflation. It discusses compatibility with prefill compression and removes the serving-framework integration limitation from Appendix F following the vLLM experiments. The limitation concerning predominantly long-input workloads remains.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's Transformers proof of concept, v2 documents vLLM v1 integration, identifying modified block-table and attention files and environment flags for switching methods (E.2). It also clarifies that dequantization overhead is included in attention timing. Core hyperparameters, pseudocode, quantization formats, and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting quantization sensitivity, Qwen3, serving evaluation, Intelligence/Watt, and vLLM integration, alongside additional quantization and sparsity citations. The research positioning in Section 1.1 and Appendix B remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The central exposition is substantially reorganized: v1 interleaves observations and procedures within Section 3, whereas v2 groups motivating analyses in Section 3 and methodology in Section 4. Formulations are renamed, evaluation discussions are rewritten and expanded, and navigation and cross-references are updated.

P2.justification: v2 adds serving, sensitivity, Pareto-front, and latency-breakdown figures and five tables, while expanding the component-ablation table with performance columns. Existing sparsity plots are exchanged between Figure 3 and the appendix, captions identify settings more explicitly, and Figure 1(c)'s axes are redrawn. These changes substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's explicit gap in optimized-serving validation through documented vLLM integration and controlled throughput/concurrent-request measurements (E.2, E.12, Figure 9). This substantially strengthens the central systems contribution. Expanded component, sensitivity, and long-context tests also improve its evidential support. Uncertainty intervals remain absent and Intelligence/Watt is underexplained, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
